subject: UK addendum + TIA routing: scope confirmation and timelines
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medwave.com>, privacy@medwave.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-28 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: UK addendum + TIA routing: scope confirmation and timelines

Hi Liam / MedWave privacy team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — good to align on the high-level safeguards you need for UK patients. To keep things moving, can you confirm two quick items so we can scope the DTIAs & UK addendum work:  

1) Jurisdiction footprint: you mentioned EU + UK + APAC support, but the DPIA indicated workloads for Ireland, Germany, UK, and Singapore. Confirm if Singapore is in-scope for the first rollout or can be deferred.
2) Processing details: are there any special log retention or routing requirements beyond pseudonymised telemetry? Specifically, do you require onshore logging for UK-only personal data?

I'm attaching a short subprocessors extract and our standard TIA template to show the level of evidence we can provide (redwood-subprocessors-2028-04.csv and tia-template-redwood-2028.docx). If both items above are clear, we can:

- Draft a UK Addendum + SCCs reference mapping (legal)
- Produce per-jurisdiction TIA/DTIA evidence package (security ops + infra)
- Share an estimated timeline (2-week DRAFT for legal + 3-week ops sprint for the evidence pack)

Proposed next steps: you confirm Singapore scope and onshore logging ask by EOD tomorrow, we kick off the internal runbook and target a DocuSign for the addendum within 3 weeks (subject to your procurement).

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman
Director, Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2028-04.csv (summary), tia-template-redwood-2028.docx (TIA template)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medwave.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@medwave.com
Date: 2028-04-28 11:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: UK addendum + TIA routing: scope confirmation and timelines

Hi Naomi / team,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few answers inline:

1) Singapore: for phase 1 we'll exclude Singapore — target rollout will be EU + UK only. Good call to defer APAC.
2) Onshore logging: MedWave requires that any event-level logs containing direct identifiers for UK residents be stored within UK/EU controls. Metadata and aggregated telemetry can be routed to our global analytics pool.

We attached the DPIA summary (medwave-dpia-2028-04-28.pdf) which highlights a narrow set of identifiers considered "direct": MRN, NHS number, and patient email.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide:  
- A routing map showing where request bodies and logs are written (region by bucket)
- A statement on whether Redwood’s subprocessors will process UK direct identifiers outside UK/EU or whether they are bound by our addendum controls

Procurement note: our legal is comfortable with SCCs + UK Addendum in principle, but will need the TIA evidence before countersignature. Timeline: procurement wants the addendum signed within 3 weeks if the TIA evidence is acceptable.

Thanks,

Liam O'Connor
Head of Privacy Operations, MedWave Health
liam.oconnor@medwave.com

Attachment: medwave-dpia-2028-04-28.pdf

Thanks Naomi — looping infra & security.

Quick internal plan:
- Karthik / infra to produce a region-by-component routing map (S3 buckets, KV cache, audit logs) and mark whether logs contain PII.
- Kimberley / security to assemble encryption/keys evidence and subprocessors attestation.
- I'll own the TIA write-up and will draft a per-claim evidence table against the DPIA items (MRN/NHS/email).

Naomi — I'll aim to get a first internal evidence packet to share with MedWave by next Wednesday (2028-05-02). If procurement expects DocuSign in 3 weeks, that timeline should be workable provided no surprises from the subprocessors extract.

> We attached the DPIA summary (medwave-dpia-2028-04-28.pdf) which highlights a narrow set of identifiers considered "direct": MRN, NHS number, and patient email.

Marissa

marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medwave.com>
Date: 2028-04-28 14:35:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: UK addendum + TIA routing: scope confirmation and timelines

Folks — technical clarifications and proposed mitigations.

1) Routing map: we'll produce a diagram that shows per-component write/read regions. Short answer: request bodies and KV cache are written to the customer-region cluster by default; long-term logs (audit and analytics) are forwarded to our central logging cluster unless a per-customer routing flag is enabled. We can enable UK-only retention for MedWave with the following changes:
   - set routing flag on the customer profile to keep event logs in London cluster (retention TTL as requested)
   - ensure KV snapshots do not include direct identifiers (we pseudonymize at ingest)

2) Subprocessors: our subprocessors CSV shows 6 named processors — three of which are EU-based storage/CDN providers and one is a US-based telemetry aggregator. For UK-direct identifiers we can enforce contractual routing: the aggregator will only receive hashed identifiers for EU/UK customers when routing flag is set; raw identifiers will be suppressed. We'll include that in the TIA.

3) TIA / DTIA approach: recommend we provide two artifacts: (A) a legal mapping (SCCs + UK IDTA addendum language) and (B) an operational DTIA that contains evidence artifacts (routing map, logs retention policy export, subprocessors attestation, encryption key custody statement). Together these satisfy procurement's ask and should unblock the DocuSign.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2028-04.csv (updated with regional processing column)

If Marissa can draft the evidence table I can slot our infra exports into it by Tuesday EOD.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: UK addendum + TIA routing: scope confirmation and timelines

Liam — thanks for the fast responses and for sharing the DPIA. Summary & next steps below so procurement has a single place to look.

Summary of commitments from Redwood (draft):
- Legal: we'll produce SCC mapping + a short UK IDTA addendum consistent with your DPIA definitions.
- Ops: provide a DTIA/evidence packet containing routing maps, logs retention export (UK-only for direct identifiers), subprocessors attestation (we'll redact commercial pricing), and key custody statement.
- Timing: Redwood internal target: legal draft by 2028-05-04; Ops evidence packet by 2028-05-09. Target DocuSign for addendum if evidence is accepted by MedWave procurement: signature window 2028-05-18 to 2028-05-22.

Action items for MedWave:
- Confirm Singapore exclusion for phase 1 (we have this from Liam but flagging for record)
- Confirm that MRN, NHS number, and patient email are the only direct identifiers that require UK-only retention (per DPIA)

I've created a HubSpot deal record and added the timeline (link below). Once you confirm, I'll send a short DocuSign placeholder for the addendum so legal can see the final clause set; procurement can then attach it to the countersign flow.

Best,

Naomi Feldman
Director, Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
